_meta.purpose: JD keyword taxonomy. Drives archetype detection in match.mjs and content scoring in tailor.mjs. atsKeywords is the vocabulary a tailored resume is graded against.
_meta.editingNote: Add a term here the moment you see it repeatedly in real JDs. devGaps is the honesty guard — it must stay truthful; if Dev genuinely learns something, remove it from devGaps AND add the fact to resume/resume-content.json.
_meta.aiRemoved: ai-agent-engineer, llm-app-engineer and fullstack-ai were removed as archetypes on 2026-09-09. Dev's agentic engineering is how he writes code, not the job he is applying for. The agentic skills stay in resume-content.json and still score for roles that value them (notably forward-deployed-engineer), but no archetype targets an AI job title any more.

devHasEvidence: Collaborated deeply with European clients (Norway, Germany, France) to build certified software — genuinely client-facing delivery, not internal-only work
Shipped under DiGA, HAS and PECAN health-compliance frameworks — comfort with regulated customer environments
Integrated complex third-party SDKs, hardware layers and real-time pipelines (VIMscore, AppThera, Garmin, Wahoo, Intervals.icu)
Full-stack breadth across Flutter, KMP, React, Node.js, Django and Rails — the generalist profile FDE hiring wants
Builds the agent tooling that compresses delivery time, which is exactly the FDE force-multiplier argument
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead with direct international client delivery under regulatory constraint, then breadth of stack, then the agent tooling as the multiplier. FDE hiring optimises for judgement + range + customer nerve, all of which he can evidence.

devHasEvidence: 2.7 years of production Flutter/Dart, including leading the Tymewear app client
BLE connectivity, real-time sensor pipelines and offline session sync — hard Flutter problems, not CRUD screens
Led architectural design of production-grade Flutter applications for international markets
Fastlane-automated App Store and Play Store releases
devGaps: Named Flutter state-management libraries (BLoC/Riverpod/GetX) are not on the resume — do not claim a specific one
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead Flutter and Dart, foreground the BLE/IoT and offline-sync depth plus release ownership, and keep the agentic work as a secondary differentiator.

devHasEvidence: Led architectural design and deployment of production KMP applications
Delivered the Lifeness client in KMP + SwiftUI against a Rails/GraphQL backend — genuine shared-code-plus-native-UI experience
Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, MVI, MVVM and Clean Architecture all in production
Managed Firebase builds and live release cycles on both stores
devGaps: Kotlin/Native or KMP for desktop/web targets
Android framework internals / custom view systems
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead Kotlin Multiplatform and SwiftUI as a shipped combination — KMP adoption is still rare, so being able to say 'delivered a certified KMP app to both stores' is the whole pitch.

devHasEvidence: Shipped across Flutter, KMP, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose and React Native — unusually broad for 2.7 years
Owns releases end to end on both App Store and Play Store, automated with Fastlane
Two production apps for international markets: Tymewear (USA) and Lifeness (Norway/Germany)
devGaps: Large-scale app performance profiling at millions-of-users scale
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead the breadth — one engineer who has shipped Flutter, KMP and SwiftUI to both stores — and back it with the two named international products.

devHasEvidence: React, Node.js and TypeScript are all on the resume as delivered full-stack work
Backend delivery in Django and Ruby on Rails with REST and GraphQL APIs consumed at scale
Full product-cycle ownership from architecture through release
devGaps: MongoDB — genuinely absent from the resume. Do NOT claim the 'M' in MERN.
Express.js is not named on the resume (Node.js is)
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead React + Node + TypeScript honestly, lean on backend delivery via Django and Rails to prove real server-side capability, and never imply MongoDB. If the JD is MongoDB-hard, flag it as a stretch.

devHasEvidence: React and React Native both on the resume
Figma-driven delivery — built /design-spec, which turns a Figma link into a Figma-to-code mapping and a pixel-accurate prototype against a codified design system
TypeScript/JavaScript in production
devGaps: Redux or a named state-management library
archetypes.summaryAngle: Frontend is his thinnest lane on paper. Lead with cross-platform UI architecture, the design-system discipline from /design-spec, and React Native as evidence of React-model fluency.

devHasEvidence: Django/Python backend services for Tymewear including REST APIs and real-time sensor pipelines
Ruby on Rails + GraphQL backend for Lifeness
Node.js on the resume as a delivered backend technology
Bidirectional third-party sync with Garmin, Wahoo and Intervals.icu
archetypes.summaryAngle: Lead with the two real backends he shipped (Django and Rails) and the integration-heavy API work, with Node.js as the JD-matching header term.

devHasEvidence: Delivered a DiGA AND PECAN certified healthcare app (Lifeness) — a genuinely rare credential
Built under DiGA, HAS and PECAN health-compliance frameworks with European clients
Chronic-disease prevention and lifestyle-tracking features with multilingual support
VIMscore patient-analytics integration
BLE/IoT biometric platform (Tymewear) with live breathing and heart-rate tracking
devGaps: HIPAA specifically (his frameworks are EU: DiGA/HAS/PECAN)
archetypes.summaryAngle: This is his most defensible niche. Lead with DiGA + PECAN certification by name — very few engineers at any level can say it — then the biometric/BLE platform.

devHasEvidence: 2.7 years of production delivery across mobile and full-stack
R&R Award for Above and Beyond Performance
Rigorous code review, Git branching strategy and technical documentation practice
devGaps: Data structures & algorithms interview prep is unproven on paper
archetypes.summaryAngle: Fallback framing when the JD is vague. Lead with breadth and shipped products, and let the agentic work be the thing that makes him memorable.

seniorityGuidance: Dev is at 2.7 years (Jan 2024 start). APPLY freely to: 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, 3-5 years, SDE-2, Software Engineer II, 'mid-level'. STRETCH — apply anyway when the stack fit is strong, because Indian JDs routinely list a number above what they will actually hire: 3-6 years, 4-6 years. SKIP: anything with Senior / Staff / Principal / Lead / Architect / Manager in the title, 6+ or 8+ year minimums, or people-management responsibility. IMPORTANT EXCEPTION for the AI/agentic lane: the field is roughly three years old, so '3-5 years of AI experience' functionally means 'has actually shipped agent systems'. Dev qualifies on substance there — apply regardless of the stated number, and make the /dev-loop and MCP work the first thing the reader sees.
